item.title: Metformin Use Before Assisted Reproductive Technology and Pregnancy Outcomes in Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Nationwide Cohort Study
item.description: Metformin has been hypothesized to improve ovulation and pregnancy rates in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) undergoing assisted reproductive technology (ART). This population-based cohort study assessed pregnancy outcomes associated with metformin use prior to ART in women with PCOS. We included 10,178 women with PCOS undergoing their first fresh embryo transfer cycle under the national health insurance program of South Korea between 2017 and 2021. Women who received metformin for...

item.title: European society for organ transplantation clinical practice guideline on prevention and treatment of chronic lung allograft dysfunction
item.description: Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) is the primary cause of late graft loss after lung transplantation, affecting up to half of lung transplant recipients within 5 years and presenting with heterogeneous phenotypes, most commonly bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS) and restrictive allograft syndrome. Prevention and treatment of CLAD are challenging. This European Society for Organ Transplantation (ESOT) clinical practice guideline was developed by a multidisciplinary Task Force,...

item.title: Implementation of the World Health Organization's Package of Essential Noncommunicable Disease Interventions: an overview of reviews
item.description: CONCLUSION: WHO PEN and similar strategies can improve NCD service delivery and outcomes, but sustained investments, context-specific adaptations, and longer-term evaluations are needed to overcome persistent implementation barriers.

item.title: Construction and multi-center validation of a model based on blending ensemble learning for predicting stroke-associated pneumonia following acute ischemic stroke
item.description: CONCLUSION: The proposed Blending ensemble model exhibits excellent generalizability and high sensitivity. The accompanying web-based tool provides robust decision support for identifying high-risk patients and implementing early precision interventions.

item.title: Socioeconomic, institutional, environmental, and demographic determinants of population health in 90 developing countries: panel data evidence
item.description: Anchored in Grossman's health production framework, this study examines how socioeconomic, institutional, environmental, and demographic conditions are associated with population health in developing countries. Population health is measured through three complementary indicators-life expectancy, infant mortality, and maternal mortality-to capture broader survival conditions, early-life vulnerability, and maternal health risks. Using panel data for 90 developing countries from 2002 to 2018, the...

item.title: Association of nutritional status assessed by the controlling nutritional status score with clinical outcomes in adults with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
item.description: CONCLUSION: The CONUT score was independently associated with 1-year all-cause mortality in adults with HFpEF and demonstrated significantly better discrimination than GNRI. Its discriminative performance was numerically higher than, but not statistically different from, that of PNI. CONUT may therefore serve as a practical supplementary tool for post-discharge risk stratification, although external validation is required.

item.title: Nerandomilast is Associated With Altered Alveolar Epithelial Cell State Dynamics While Attenuating Fibrotic Remodeling in Pulmonary Fibrosis
item.description: Pulmonary fibrosis is a progressive and life-threatening lung disorder characterized by excessive fibrogenesis and impaired respiratory function. Nerandomilast, a preferential phosphodiesterase 4B inhibitor, is currently approved for the treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and progressive pulmonary fibrosis in several countries following its demonstrated clinical efficacy in Phase III trials. However, its cellular mechanisms of action remain incompletely understood. In this study, we...

item.title: The association between systemic inflammation as measured by calprotectin and autoantibody load in rheumatoid arthritis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Plasma calprotectin is positively associated with seropositivity and AMPA load by autoantibody levels and the breadth of the autoantibody response.

item.title: REST in the Central Nervous System: Context-Dependent Regulation of Neuronal Homeostasis and Disease
item.description: The RE1-silencing transcription factor (REST), also known as neuron-restrictive silencer factor (NRSF), is a zinc-finger domain-containing transcriptional regulator involved in coordinating gene expression programmes in the nervous system. Initially characterized as a repressor of neuronal genes in nonneuronal cells, REST also exerts context-dependent functions during neurodevelopment, neuronal maturation, homeostasis and brain ageing. Its activity involves the recruitment of multiple regulatory...

item.title: A Csi-miR3954b-CsCE70/CsPLA1 Regulatory Module Enhances Citrus Fruit Resistance to Penicillium digitatum by Promoting Phenolic Acid and Flavonoid Biosynthesis
item.description: Green mould is one of the major postharvest diseases affecting citrus. Although evidence indicates that microRNAs (miRNAs) participate in plant defence responses, their roles and regulatory mechanisms in citrus resistance to green mould remain unclear. Small RNA sequencing identified several defence-associated miRNAs involved in citrus resistance to Penicillium digitatum. Among them, transient overexpression screening identified Csi-miR3954b as the most effective miRNA, reducing disease...

item.title: A Conceptual Roadmap toward Informed Prenatal Genetic Screening and Diagnostic Testing: A Qualitative Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that supporting prenatal genetic testing decisions requires more than standardized counseling and underscores the importance of understanding patients' preferences for decision making and information delivery. These preferences should be considered alongside factors such as reproductive history and maternal age, which may further shape how testing options and outcomes are understood. Together, these findings reinforce the need for a more individualized approach...

item.title: A Health-Protective Screening Threshold for Personal Care Products: Metabolomic and Endocrine Mechanisms of Adolescent Reproductive Toxicity in Zebrafish
item.description: Adolescents are uniquely vulnerable to endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) due to the critical maturation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis, yet current safety assessments overlook whole-formulation risks during this developmental window. Using an adolescent zebrafish model, we established a biologically anchored screening threshold and elucidated the molecular mechanisms of formulation toxicity. Direct exposure to personal care products at unadjusted Scientific Committee on...

item.title: Cochlear morphology is correlated with endocranial volume in catarrhine primates
item.description: The cochlear dimensions relevant to hearing capability generally follow a pattern of allometric scaling with body mass in mammals. Nevertheless, humans exhibit cochlear dimensions larger than expected from the body mass, and it has been proposed that this is related to encephalization. In this study, we investigate whether the link between brain mass and cochlear morphology is unique to humans and whether cranial features other than brain mass impinge on the cochlear morphology in catarrhine...

item.title: Multicenter, Multivendor Development and Validation of Automated Liver Prescription
item.description: BACKGROUND: Manual prescription of liver MRI volumes introduces inter-operator variability and prolongs exam duration. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based prescription has been demonstrated, but existing work has been limited to single-vendor settings.

item.description: No abstract

item.title: A Novel De Novo MTM1 Insertion Frameshift Variant Causes X-Linked Myotubular Myopathy in a Chinese Female
item.description: CONCLUSION: This case expands the MTM1 variant spectrum and highlights that de novo MTM1 frameshift variants can underlie clinically significant XLMTM manifestations in females, underscoring the value of genetic testing in symptomatic women with centronuclear myopathy features.

item.title: Validating a New-Generation Wrist-Worn Alcohol Biosensor Among Persons With and Without HIV in a Laboratory Setting
item.description: CONCLUSION: In light of the fixed dosing procedure, peak-based correlations reflect comparisons that limit BrAC variability to a narrow band, thereby constraining TAC-BrAC correlations. TAC and BrAC were significantly correlated, with the strongest concordance observed using full time-series data. Findings suggest similarities and differences in TAC-BrAC relationships by HIV status depending on metric. Individual factors including age, race/ethnicity, HIV, and AUDIT score were associated with...

item.title: The Changing Landscape of Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: Aligning Access With the Clinical Obesity Framework
item.description: Metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) is the most effective treatment for severe obesity, yet it remains profoundly underutilized. Patients seeking MBS face pretreatment requirements, including mandatory psychological evaluation, documented failed diet attempts, and months of lifestyle interventions that are substantially more extensive than those required for most common gastrointestinal procedures. These requirements were initially developed with patient safety in mind, but evidence has...

item.title: DUSP4 activates adipocyte thermogenesis via CRTC3 dephosphorylation-dependent UCP1 expression
item.description: Obesity arises when a chronic energy surplus overwhelms the storage capacity of adipocytes and subsequently causes systemic metabolic dysfunction. Adaptive thermogenesis, primarily mediated by uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1) in adipocytes, serves to counteract obesity by dissipating excess energy as heat. Despite extensive studies on thermogenic regulation, the phosphatases that regulate this protective metabolic pathway remain poorly understood. Here we identify dual-specificity phosphatase 4...

item.title: Pathological calcium overload impairs skeletal muscle regeneration through sustained NFAT-dependent proliferative signaling
item.description: Skeletal muscle regeneration requires coordinated myoblast proliferation and differentiation. Calcium dysregulation is commonly observed in aging and disease-associated muscle weakness; however, its impact on myogenic progression remains unclear. In this study, we investigated the mechanism by which intracellular calcium overload impairs myogenic differentiation and muscle regeneration. Transcriptomic analysis of aged human muscle revealed coordinated activation of calcium signaling and...

item.title: Single-cell epigenomics of colorectal cancer
item.description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) exhibits remarkable phenotypic heterogeneity that cannot be fully explained by genetic alterations alone. Advances in single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing have revealed chromatin accessibility as a central regulatory layer shaping tumor identity, cellular plasticity and therapeutic response. In this Review, we synthesize recent single-cell epigenomic studies to outline an emerging regulatory principle for CRC. From an epigenetic...

item.title: Classical Algorithms for Estimating Expectation Values in Linear Optical Circuits
item.description: We present a classical algorithm for approximating the expectation values of observables in linear optical circuits with arbitrary product input states, achieving additive-error accuracy. This result indicates that current applications of photonic systems aimed at demonstrating practical quantum advantage through expectation value estimation, such as photonic variational algorithms, may face challenges in attaining the computational advantage. It also implies the output probabilities of boson...

item.title: SERINC2: From membrane lipid synthesis to human disease
item.description: AIMS: This review aims to summarize current evidence on the role of serine incorporator 2 (SERINC2) in human disease, focusing on how its function in serine-associated membrane lipid biosynthesis-particularly phosphatidylserine and sphingolipid metabolism-may contribute to disease-associated phenotypes across cancer, cardiovascular disease, and neuropsychiatric disorders.

item.title: Neuroprotective eremophilane sesquiterpenoids from Ligularia species attenuate glutamate-induced oxidative stress via MAPK signaling
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Among the three Ligularia species examined, the highest levels of neuroprotective eremophilane sesquiterpenoids were found in L. taquetii, and taquetins C and G (3 and 7) attenuated glutamate-induced oxidative neuronal injury through modulation of MAPK signaling. These findings support the traditional anti-inflammatory use of Ligularia species as a rational starting point for the discovery of neuroprotective constituents and identify L. taquetii as a source of eremophilane...

item.title: Conceptual design of a monochromated scanning electron microscopy-based reflection electron energy loss spectroscopy system for surface nanospectroscopy
item.description: This study presents a monochromated scanning electron microscopy-based reflection electron energy loss spectroscopy (MC-SEM-REELS) system using cylindrical lenses as energy dispersive units for surface spectroscopy at the nanoscale. After examining the validity of the theory through comparisons with the experimental results in our previous studies, we estimated the theoretical performance and limitations of the MC-SEM-REELS system based on electron-optical simulation. The results reveal that the...

item.title: The effect of intermittent theta burst stimulation on central poststroke pain: A pilot randomized controlled trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: iTBS was effective in reducing CPSP. Considering the safety and convenience of application, iTBS can be suggested as an effective treatment for patients with CPSP.

item.title: Accurate determination of vitamin B<sub>12</sub> in infant formula using isotope dilution-ultrahigh-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry
item.description: A method for the accurate determination of vitamin B(12) (cobalamin) in infant formula was developed using isotope dilution-liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (ID-LC-MS/MS). As an internal standard, a [^(13)C(7)]-cyanocobalamin isotope-labeled analogue was used. Because of the hygroscopic property of cobalamins, the concentration of the cyanocobalamin standard solution was determined via quantitative nuclear magnetic resonance (qNMR) spectroscopy and further validated by capillary...

item.title: Machine-learning-based model for motional Stark effect calibrations
item.description: The motional Stark effect (MSE) diagnostic on the Korea Superconducting Tokamak Advanced Research (KSTAR) device requires a beam-into-gas calibration to remove the Faraday-rotation contribution to the measured polarization angle. Because the secondary-neutral emission that contaminates this calibration grows with the torus gas pressure, the calibration is obtained by measuring the polarization angle over a range of pressures at a fixed vacuum field and extrapolating to zero pressure. Such...

item.title: Correction: Improving insulin resistance by sulforaphane via activating the Bacteroides and Lactobacillus SCFAs-GPR-GLP1 signal axis
item.description: Correction for 'Improving insulin resistance by sulforaphane via activating the Bacteroides and Lactobacillus SCFAs-GPR-GLP1 signal axis' by Sicong Tian et al., Food Funct., 2024, 15, 8644-8660, https://doi.org/10.1039/d4fo01059k.

item.title: Morphological identification of Dendritobilharzia sp. (Schistosomatidae) from a Whooper Swan in the Republic of Korea
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This paper reports the first record of Dendritobilharzia from an avian host in the Republic of Korea and provides baseline data on the avian schistosome distribution. These findings improve the understanding of parasite diversity and host-parasite relationships and support future studies on wildlife health and transmission.

item.title: Lean-lithium solid-state electrolytes through interfacial percolation
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Spatial transcriptomic profiling of porcine tissue microarray detecting subclinical circovirus infection
item.description: Porcine Circovirus type 2 (PCV2) is a key pathogen in pigs that induces host immunosuppression, leading to severe secondary infections such as porcine circovirus-associated disease (PCVAD), resulting in significant economic losses for the swine industry. More recently, it has emerged as a pathogen that needs to be ruled out in porcine xenotransplantation research due to issues related to latent infection. In this study, we established a methodology for distinguishing cell types and detecting the...

item.title: Lee Byeong-haeng's Taegeuk Acupuncture and the Debate over the Modernization of Korean Medicine
item.description: This study examines the life and scholarly achievements of Lee Byeong-haeng (1906-1975), who passed the Qualifying Examination for Korean Medical Doctors in 1954 and subsequently established himself as both a clinician and a theorist. By exploring one dimension of the debate over the "modernization" of traditional Korean medicine in which Lee played a significant role, the study seeks to illuminate the intellectual shifts that shaped the 1960s and 1970s, formative decades in the development of...

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Associations between maternal sleep disorders and long-term neurodevelopmental disorders in children: evidence from a national cohort of 1.9 million births
item.description: CONCLUSION: Maternal SD before or during pregnancy is independently associated with increased LNDD risk in offspring.

item.title: Golgi dysfunction in Alzheimer disease: from human multiomic signatures to therapeutic targets
item.description: Deciphering the intricate pathogenesis of Alzheimer disease (AD) has been a highly demanding task for researchers for decades. Evidence from from human multiomic studies provides critical insights into complex disease mechanisms and drives novel findings. However, the data are often selectively comprehended, leaving a few notable factors underappreciated in the research field. We focus on the Golgi apparatus, one of the most undervalued organelles in AD research, to demonstrate its...

item.title: Transparent 3D-printable biointeractive surfaces enable real-time oral biofilm investigation under controlled flow
item.description: OBJECTIVE: To identify a transparent, directly 3D-printable material (CYTO) capable of recapitulating hydroxyapatite (HA)-associated bacterial attachment while enabling real-time microfluidic investigation of oral biofilms under controlled flow conditions.

item.title: Assessment of Acute Functional Effects of Perfluorooctanoic Acid (PFOA), Heptafluorobutyric Acid (HFBA), and Hexafluoropropylene Oxide Dimer Acid (HFPO-DA) in Human iPSC-Derived Cardiomyocytes Using Multielectrode Arrays
item.description: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are persistent environmental pollutants associated with public health risks. The cardiac electrophysiological effects of the representative long-chain PFAS perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and short-chain PFASs such as heptafluorobutyric acid (HFBA) and hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA) remain insufficiently understood. In this study, the electrophysiological effects of PFASs were evaluated in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived...

item.title: lncRNA H19 downregulation mediates oxidative stress-induced osteogenic dysfunction
item.description: Age-related bone loss results from an imbalance between bone resorption and formation, which is heavily influenced by senescence of osteoblasts. Oxidative stress and the associated production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) are key contributors to bone aging and impaired bone formation. Our previous study demonstrated that protein arginine deiminase 2 (PADI2) is downregulated by ROS, leading to cellular senescence and impaired osteoblast differentiation. In this study, lncRNA H19 was identified...

item.title: Impact of Repeated Endobiliary Radiofrequency Ablation on Survival in Unresectable Perihilar Cholangiocarcinoma
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Endobiliary RFA was associated with improved survival in unresectable perihilar CCA, with the benefit concentrated in the first three months after biliary drainage, at the cost of more frequent non-tumor biliary obstruction.

item.title: The burden and long-term outcomes of diagnosed and underdiagnosed COPD across diverse communities from high-income, middle-income, and low-income countries: the Prospective Urban Rural Epidemiology (PURE) study
item.description: BACKGROUND: Airflow obstruction detected on spirometry is a hallmark of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and is needed for the diagnosis of COPD. Sparse data in high-income countries (HICs) have reported high prevalence of underdiagnosed COPD with poor clinical outcomes. Data are missing for low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs) to inform the burden and clinical outcomes of underdiagnosed COPD.

item.title: Quantitative FP-CIT PET analysis of dopaminergic degeneration in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder and early Parkinson's disease
item.description: CONCLUSION: Regional quantitative ^(18)F-FP-CIT PET reveals intermediate dopaminergic dysfunction in iRBD and highlights early posterior putamen involvement as a potential imaging marker. Quantitative PET metrics predicted phenoconversion comparably to expert visual interpretation while providing objective, continuous measures that enable individual-level risk stratification.

item.title: Interactions between pharmaceutically active compounds and organic foulants in ultrafiltration processes
item.description: In this study, we systematically investigated the fundamental interactions between pharmaceutically active compounds (PhACs) and organic fouling layers during ultrafiltration (UF) processes. Two representative PhACs, propranolol (PRP) and naproxen (NPX), were filtered through polyethersulfone membranes fouled with natural organic matter surrogates, including humic acid, bovine serum albumin, and sodium alginate. The results suggested that electrostatic interactions contributed substantially to...

item.title: Growth and fixed mindsets and later exhaustion-cynicism in adolescents: Prospective associations involving goal clarity/commitment and self-regulated learning
item.description: Exhaustion and cynicism are central symptoms of academic burnout. This study examined prospective associations between adolescents' growth and fixed mindsets and later exhaustion-cynicism symptoms, including indirect associations involving goal clarity/commitment and self-regulated learning (SRL). Three waves of the Seoul Education Longitudinal Study (SELS) were analyzed using a baseline-adjusted structural equation model involving 1999 Grade 10 students. Wave 1 mindsets were modeled as...

item.title: Asymmetric behavioral responses to changes in subjective survival expectations: Implications for health investment in later life
item.description: OBJECTIVES: Subjective survival probability (SSP) is a key predictor of economic and health decisions in later life, yet existing research assumes that gains and losses in survival expectations have symmetric behavioral effects. This study examines how within-person changes in SSP are associated with health-promoting behaviors among middle-aged and older adults in South Korea.

item.title: Type II RAF Inhibitor Tovorafenib in Recurrent/Refractory Melanoma or Other Solid Tumors With BRAF Fusions or CRAF/RAF1 Fusions or Amplification: Phase II FIRELIGHT-1 Substudy
item.description: CONCLUSION: Tovorafenib demonstrated single-agent clinical activity in solid tumors with BRAF fusions or CRAF fusions or amplification and had a manageable safety profile. Tovorafenib may offer a new targeted treatment option for adult patients with tumors harboring these rare genomic driver alterations.

item.title: Concordance of p16 status between US-guided core needle biopsy and surgical specimens in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma: A diagnostic accuracy study
item.description: With the increasing prevalence of human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), there is a need for efficient, minimally invasive methods to evaluate p16 status. This study aimed to assess the concordance of p16 status between ultrasound (US)-guided core needle biopsy (CNB) of cervical lymph nodes and surgical specimens, and to describe the numbers of CNB and surgical sessions required to establish the histopathologic diagnosis. This retrospective study...

item.title: Oral health behaviors, perceptions, and educational needs among enlisted South Korean Army soldiers during the COVID-19 pandemic: A cross-sectional study
item.description: Preventive oral health care and education are essential for soldiers' health and military readiness. This study investigated oral health behaviors, dental service utilization, oral health perceptions, and educational needs among enlisted South Korean Army soldiers during the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 313 enlisted soldiers who visited military dental clinics in Gyeonggi-do, Republic of Korea, from March 24 to April 16, 2021. Descriptive...

item.title: Echocardiographic factors suggestive of pulmonary hypertension in patients with mediastinal tumors: A single-center observational study
item.description: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) may occur in diverse clinical contexts. Group 5 PH includes conditions with unclear or multifactorial mechanisms, including tumor-associated PH. Evidence regarding the frequency and clinical significance of elevated right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) in patients with mediastinal tumors (MT) is limited. This study aimed to identify clinical and echocardiographic factors associated with elevated RVSP suggestive of PH in patients with MT. This retrospective...

item.title: Long-term integrative personalized medicine care in massive brainstem hemorrhage: A CARE-compliant case report
item.description: RATIONALE: Brainstem hemorrhage is a rare but devastating subtype of intracerebral hemorrhage that frequently presents with impaired consciousness, quadriplegia, and recurrent infections. Integrative personalized medicine care (IPMC), which combines essential conventional treatments with personalized traditional Korean medicine interventions, has been suggested to improve functional outcomes and support immune regulation. By closely monitoring a patient with massive brainstem hemorrhage treated...

item.title: The landscape of allele-specific expression in human kidneys
item.description: Allele-specific expression (ASE), the preferential expression of one gene copy, is a key mechanism of genomic regulation. However, its role in human kidney disease remains poorly understood. In this study, we generated a high-quality, genome-wide ASE map using paired whole-genome sequencing and RNA sequencing from microdissected glomerular and tubulointerstitial compartments of patients with proteinuric kidney disease. We showed that the majority of common ASE events were deterministic and...

item.title: Smoking Cessation Duration and Diabetic Microvascular Complications
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this retrospective cohort study of patients with diabetes, smoking cessation for 8 or more years was associated with a lower risk of all diabetic microvascular complications, diabetic nephropathy, retinopathy, and neuropathy compared with continuous smoking. These associations were observed mainly among male participants, underscoring the potential importance of sustained long-term smoking cessation for microvascular risk reduction.

item.title: Sex Differences in Mortality Among Patients With Hepatocellular Carcinoma
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, sex disparities in HCC mortality existed but were heterogeneous across ethnic background and liver disease etiologies. These findings support incorporation of sex-based considerations in HCC management.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence in High-resolution Anorectal Manometry: Current Applications and Future Directions
item.description: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: High-resolution anorectal manometry (HRAM) has improved anorectal physiological assessment but remains limited by conventional pressure-based metrics that incompletely reflect the complex spatiotemporal physiology of continence and defecation. This review summarizes recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning and their potential to enhance HRAM interpretation and clinical decision-making.

item.title: Correction: Regorafenib as Second-Line Versus Later-Line Therapy in Advanced Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multicenter Real-World Study with Exploratory Analysis of Prior Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Exposure
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Associations between weather variables and sleep architecture: A large-scale analysis using consumer sleep data
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Temperature, humidity, and sunshine duration were significantly associated with sleep structure. These effects may be less pronounced in individuals with sleep-disordered breathing.

item.title: Development and Validation of Human-AI Collaborative Workflow in SNOMED CT Mapping of Bilingual Clinical Text
item.description: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine-Clinical Terminology (SNOMED CT) is the principal international standard for semantic interoperability of clinical information, but mapping free-text clinical narratives to SNOMED CT concepts remains labor-intensive. We developed a large language model agent system for mapping bilingual clinical text to SNOMED CT concepts and evaluated its effect on mapping accuracy and efficiency within a human-AI collaborative workflow. We designed a three-module agent...

item.title: Stent-assisted coil embolization for a thrombosed giant coronary aneurysm in IgG4-related coronary arteritis: a 2-year follow-up
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Intention to complete advance directives among patients with cancer undergoing treatment: application of the extended theory of planned behavior
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the Extended Theory of Planned Behavior as a useful framework for understanding advance directive completion among cancer patients. Perceived behavioral control was identified as the strongest predictor of intention, underscoring the importance of enhancing patients' confidence and ability to engage in advance care planning. The results suggest that structured counseling and tailored education should be initiated early in the treatment process to support...

item.title: Multi-threshold synaptic transistor for an artificial sensory-pain integrated receptor
item.description: Pain is a simple yet effective self-defense mechanism in humans that enables rapid responses to harmful stimuli. The inability to sense pain increases the risk of injury due to delayed reactions to such stimuli. However, current prostheses often struggle to differentiate between sensory and pain-like signals and require complex systems to achieve this functionality. In this study, we developed an artificial receptor capable of detecting both sensory and pain-like signals with the threshold...

item.title: Culture-Agnostic and Culture-Specific Analyses of Semantic Fluency in Korean and English Speakers With Alzheimer's Disease
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The present findings suggest that culturally grounded schemas may influence both word generation and the organization of clustering and switching in semantic fluency. In Korean-speaking individuals with AD, zodiac animals formed structured clusters and switches that uniquely correlated with global cognition, highlighting the need for culturally informed norms in cross-linguistic neuropsychological assessment.

item.title: Changes in major global trade centers: Based on a visual assessment method
item.description: This paper uses a network model to analyze the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on global trade centers. Using import-export trade data from 12 major economies, we visually assess the shifts in global trade network positions before and after the pandemic. By constructing a balanced trade network for the years 2018, 2019, and 2020, we examine how the pandemic has affected the trade connections of key countries. Our study finds that China maintained positive growth and strengthened its trade ties...

item.title: Guest-induced amorphization and cage-selective guest dynamics in solid organic clathrates
item.description: Solid-state host-guest reactions, in which a crystalline solid transforms upon direct uptake of a gaseous guest, represent a class of phase transformation whose molecular-scale mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we exploit xenon-loaded hydroquinone clathrates as a model system to reveal the molecular mechanisms governing both the formation pathway and the cage-filling behavior of solid host-guest materials, by combining structural analysis, spectroscopy, kinetic modeling, and molecular...

item.title: Clinical Importance and Usefulness of Direct Targeting of the Ventral Intermediate Nucleus of the Thalamus Using Fluid and White Matter Suppression Imaging at 3T MRI
item.description: CONCLUSION: Direct image-based targeting of the Vim using FLAWS imaging at 3T MRI is feasible and offers practical advantages by improving initial targeting accuracy and reducing the need for target realignments in the MRgFUS procedure.

item.title: LiCl-assisted electrophoretic deposition of dense ionic covalent organic framework membranes for rapid Li<sup>+</sup>/Mg<sup>2+</sup> separation
item.description: LiCl-assisted electrophoretic deposition rapidly assembles sulfonated covalent organic framework nanosheets into dense membranes, enabling fast Li^(+) transport with Li^(+)/Mg^(2+) separation factors up to 242 in binary simulated salt-lake brines.

item.title: The Association Between General Health Literacy and Oral Health Among Korean Adults
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that inadequate HL is independently associated with poorer oral health outcomes and reduced dental care utilization, particularly in Asian contexts where oral health literacy interventions remain limited.

item.title: Hypertonic Dextrose in Aesthetic Dermatology: Route-Dependent Evidence, Biological Rationale, and Research Priorities
item.description: CONCLUSION: Hypertonic dextrose should be regarded as an investigational, route-dependent adjunct rather than an established stand-alone biostimulant. Controlled trials should isolate device, vehicle, osmolarity, and glucose-specific effects and include objective structural endpoints and long-term safety follow-up.

item.title: Differences in the rates of bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest resulting in favourable neurological outcomes according to the regional deprivation index
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Although high-deprivation regions had lower BCPR rates, the association between BCPR and favourable neurological outcomes was stronger in high-deprivation regions than in moderate- and low-deprivation regions. Multifaceted interventions are needed to increase BCPR rates in highly deprived regions.

item.title: Ultrasound-Guided Distal Thoracolumbar Fascia Hydrodissection at the Gluteal Junction: A Technical Report With Cadaveric Assessment of Compartmental Spread and Gross Neural Sparing
item.description: Chronic low back pain with radiating lower-extremity symptoms in the absence of clear radiculopathy or major central canal stenosis remains a common diagnostic and therapeutic challenge. In patients with radiating low back pain without a convincing compressive correlate, posterior myofascial structures may be considered among several potential contributors; however, the present report evaluates the anatomical feasibility of a distal thoracolumbar fascia (TLF) hydrodissection approach rather than...

item.title: National Overview of Designated Infectious Disease Control Institutions and Medical Response Resources in the Republic of Korea, 2025
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Medical response resources varied by region and hospital size, with negative-pressure isolation beds, critical care equipment, and specialized personnel concentrated in larger hospitals and select regions. These findings reveal that infectious disease response capacity should be assessed not only by the number of designated institutions but also by the distribution and availability of medical resources.

item.title: Predictors of low birth weight deliveries at a primary health care facility: Suhum Government Hospital, Ghana - a retrospective cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this single-facility study, late ANC initiation and fewer than two TD doses were associated with higher odds of LBW, while adequate haemoglobin at 36 weeks and normal BMI were associated with lower odds. Strengthening timely ANC, maternal anaemia monitoring and management and completion of recommended maternal immunisation may be relevant to similar primary healthcare settings; larger multicentre studies are needed to assess generalisability.

item.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis prevalence and infection intensity among school-going children in Timor-Leste after the prolonged interruption of deworming: a cross-sectional survey (2025)
item.description: BACKGROUND: Timor-Leste reduced soil-transmitted helminth (STH) prevalence from 29% to 18% by 2020 through mass drug administration (MDA) in 2015-2019. School-based deworming was interrupted for nearly four years during the COVID-19 pandemic and resumed in 2022 in 3 municipalities and nationwide in 2024. We aimed to estimate STH prevalence, geographical distribution and associated factors following the re-introduction of MDA.

item.title: Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Nuclear Medicine Research, Education, and Clinical Practice: Results from a 2025 Society-Wide Survey
item.description: CONCLUSION: Generative AI showed a high adoption rate among the survey respondents, with higher perceived usefulness in research/education than in clinical practice. Given the widespread real-world use of third-party generative AI tools, our findings underscore the need for institutional guidance and privacy-aware governance to ensure safe clinical adoption.

item.title: Inter-Assay Difference of Parathyroid Hormone Radioimmunoassay in Fine-Needle Aspirate from Neck Nodules According to Nodular Component

item.description: CONCLUSION: MRI-guided personalized tDCS planning improved modeled EF delivery to the cortical swallowing target and revealed significant deviations from conventional C5/C6 placement in patients with severe PSD. item.title: Sport participation and healthy aging among older adults: a social ecological analysis of individual, contextual, and policy mechanisms
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Population aging has made healthy aging a key public health priority. This study examined the association between sport participation and healthy aging among older adults and explored its social ecological mechanisms.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In Korean adults aged ≥40 years with T2DM, underweight consistently predicted higher CKD risk, particularly in middle-aged men, whereas the association of excess adiposity with CKD differed by age and sex. These findings may help explain previously inconsistent associations between obesity and CKD risk.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Converting AI-segmented dental hard- and soft-tissue data into a realistic hybrid 3D tissue model was feasible and significantly reduced mean apical and angular inter-operator deviations, with the ordinal benefit most evident for angular positioning. These findings support further prospective evaluation of the PIM workflow.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Admission LGI was independently associated with adverse outcomes, showed better discrimination than admission glucose, and improved sPESI discrimination. External validation is required.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The authors developed an internally validated, easily applicable risk score for predicting aneurysm-related events in ADPKD patients. Generalization requires caution because of potential selection bias, and external validation is warranted.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The dashboard application demonstrates that health data collected in accordance with FHIR standards can be integrated and presented in a form suitable for disaster response. item.description: CONCLUSION: Appetite loss during chemotherapy was associated with reduced dietary intake and lower QOL. Taste alterations were closely associated with appetite loss. item.title: Why metabolism remains implicit in cognitive models
item.description: Explicitly modeling metabolic constraints remains rare in cognitive neuroscience due to methodological, empirical, and conceptual challenges. Although metabolic limits already shape the biological data that many models are fitted to, direct measurements of energetic costs remain scarce and difficult to relate to model variables. We argue that recent experimental and computational advances may soon enable more explicit integration of metabolism into cognitive models.

item.description: Drawing on formal models and empirical studies of collective decision-making in animal groups, we show that egalitarian systems can emerge and remain stable despite persistent individual inequalities in needs, information, and social position. Egalitarianism is best understood as a dynamic regulation of influence under heterogeneous conditions, where leadership is conditional, distributed, and reversible rather than fixed or coercive.

item.title: Early multimodal vasopressor strategy in septic shock: results of the TRICYCLE randomized controlled trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: Early multimodal vasopressor therapy with Ang II, vasopressin and norepinephrine in patients with septic shock demonstrated promising physiological effects. These findings provide a rationale for a larger trial to assess whether early multimodal vasopressor therapy improves patient-centered outcomes.

item.title: Dual legacy of plant water-deficit-tolerance and watering history shapes rhizosphere microbial transplant outcomes in tomato post-drought recovery
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These results indicate that the legacy of rhizosphere microbiomes shaped by host water-deficit-tolerance and irrigation history is associated with enhanced post-drought recovery, involving the enrichment of specific microbial taxa and functional guilds. The concept of dual legacy provides a useful framework for understanding microbiome-mediated plant resilience.

item.title: Daily image-guided carbon ion stereotactic radiotherapy of hepatocellular carcinoma: paving the way for MR-guided online adaptive treatment
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Daily CT- and MR-guided CISR is feasible in the liver, and demonstrates frequent violations of initial treatment planning objectives when non-adaptive or offline adaptive approaches are followed. DOA could improve target coverage and OAR protection, while particularities of carbon ions such as overdoses far from the target should be considered.

item.title: Strengthening undergraduate dental public health education in Iran: insights from national symposia
item.description: Three national symposia used consultation and consensus-building to identify core challenges in Iran's undergraduate Dental Public Health (DPH) education: Infrastructure, Workforce, Curriculum, Research, and Community engagement. Solutions called for systemic reforms prioritizing robust infrastructure, adequate workforce, and strong community links. This commentary presents insights and implications from these symposia.

item.title: Joint Developmental Trajectories of Irritability and Executive Function: Associations with Time-varying Psychopathological Problems among Chinese Adolescents
item.description: Existing research has established that irritability and executive function (EF) are distinct yet often co-occurring transdiagnostic symptoms, each with its developmental trajectory. However, no evidence exists on whether these two symptoms follow joint developmental patterns or on which patterns increase risk for later problems.
